discoveries: For legacy/v0 transactions, priority fees are charged from requested compute-unit limit times CU price, not actual consumed compute; overspecified CU limits cost money.
The current official page documents v1 transaction behavior: ComputeBudget instructions are no-ops for configuration and the message carries limits/configuration directly.
Duplicate instructions of the same compute-budget variant cause transaction failure for legacy/v0 processing; execution budget also has a 1.4M CU cap.
patterns: distinguish requested CU limit from consumed units
derive fee estimate from exact message/runtime version and reconcile to finalized meta.fee
sources.overlap: Veritas decodes legacy/v0 compute-budget instructions and calculates priority fee from CU price and limit. Its output type is legacy|0. Official docs now describe v1 message-level fee configuration. This suggests a compatibility gap in that decoder, but the impact on all fee/accounting paths has not been proven; canonical ingestion separately retains transaction meta.fee.
risks: a v1 message may be rejected or misclassified by this decoder
fee projections may omit a message-level priority fee if routed through unsupported parsing
canonical actual transaction fee remains authoritative over estimates
validation: add v1 wire fixtures against an official SDK/runtime version
prove the decoder's output and failure behavior before a code change
compare estimated fees with confirmed meta.fee including failed transactions
route any financial semantic patch through Astra Protocol/Risk independent review

provenance: Local Truth-X and execution economics source review
discoveries: The documented network fee is base signature fee plus prioritization fee, and is charged whether a transaction succeeds or fails.
Base fee counts transaction signatures and supported precompile signatures; priority fee formula rounds micro-lamports up, while v1 stores an absolute total priority fee in the message.
Jito tips and venue/protocol fees are separate economic components; net outcome accounting should not collapse them into one network-fee field.
patterns: store observed total fee and version-specific fee components separately
keep tips and venue fees distinct
sources.overlap: Truth-X captures raw transaction `meta.fee`; execution economics exposes base/priority/tip components; paper simulator uses independent configured values. End-to-end version-aware reconciliation across failed trades, tips and venue fees is not demonstrated by this source review.
risks: estimated fee and realized network fee can diverge
unsuccessful transactions still incur network fees
fee schema may not represent future transaction versions
validation: fixture success and failure fees, signature/precompile counts, v0 and v1 fee models
reconcile separate Jito tip transfers and venue fees to account deltas
prove all-in net PnL has no double count or omission

discoveries: Solana publishes production checks across RPC usage, transactions, operations and monitoring; a reachable endpoint or successful build is not a production-readiness result.
SYLPH's current recorded operational blockers include stale/overflowed Core feed, stale RPC evidence, duplicate legacy Terminal processes and unavailable configured adapters.

The project has an explicit Start SYLPH check and read-only live status audit, but existing listeners predate some source-level ownership fixes, so checkout state and running-process state must be reported separately.
